headline: LUTNICK'S DETAIL
dek: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reassigned export-enforcement agents to his personal security detail, The Atlantic reports. Commerce says it was temporary.

items.title: THE AGENTS
items.text: Bureau of Industry and Security agents, whose work includes stopping illegal exports of AI chips. BIS has fewer than 200 special agents.

items.title: THE DETAIL
items.text: They traveled on his private jet and guarded his residences, according to five people familiar. Typically three or four were on Lutnick at a time, two former officials said.

items.title: THE REQUEST
items.text: In April, Lutnick asked Congress for 290 more enforcement officers to fight chip smuggling.

items.title: COMMERCE SAYS
items.text: The assignments were temporary and meant to add protection amid credible threats.

means.label: The stakes:
means.text: Lawmakers have questioned why Lutnick hasn't done more to stop illegal Nvidia chip sales, The Atlantic reports.

means.label: The trend:
means.text: The annualized rate of public export penalties and enforcement actions roughly halved vs. 2023-24, per The Export Practitioner data The Atlantic cited.

means.label: The other side:
means.text: Commerce says the agents added protection amid credible threats.

sources: Sources: The Atlantic, Nov. 24 (five people familiar; The Export Practitioner data); Commerce Department statement.
